question: How high were the pillars?
summary: 1 Kings 7:15 (paralleled by 2 Kings 25:17 and Jeremiah 52:21) gives the bronze pillars Jachin and Boaz a height of 18 cubits each. 2 Chronicles 3:15 reports them as 35 cubits high. The Chronicler's figure nearly doubles the Kings figure for the same two pillars.

reconcile.connective: Defenders read the Chronicler's 35 as the two pillars' combined length, so each is about 17½ cubits, rounded to 18 in Kings.

discrepancy.connective: Steve Wells, in the Skeptic's Annotated Bible, presses the figures at face value: Kings gives each pillar as eighteen cubits, Chronicles as thirty-five, and the same two pillars cannot be both.

pd_work.note: Treats this exact pair, harmonizing 2 Chronicles 3:15's thirty-five cubits as the two pillars' joint length (each seventeen and a half, rounded to eighteen). Haley's specific-passage coverage could not be confirmed, so a row-surfaced harmonizing commentator keyed to the passage is used per spec.

link.note: No allowlisted page (gotquestions.org / carm.org / defendinginerrancy.com) squarely engages the 18-vs-35 pillar-height tension: GotQuestions' Jachin-and-Boaz page cites only 1 Kings and never 2 Chronicles 3:15 or the discrepancy; defendinginerrancy 1_Kings_7.15 / 2_Chronicles_3.15 both 404; CARM's only on-point article is the molten-sea (1 Kings 7:23) circumference, a different difficulty. Link omitted rather than guessed.

excerpts.excerpt_text: In Ch2 3:15 they are said to have been thirty-five cubits high. There, however, their joint lengths are given; whereas here the length of the pillars is given separately. Each pillar was seventeen and a half cubits long, which is stated, in round numbers, as eighteen.
excerpts.on_tension_rationale: Names both verses and states the dominant joint-length harmonization in full: 35 = combined, ~17.5 each, rounded to 18. Strongest single reconcile; parity-capped to one on a discrepancy_first row.
excerpts.source_note_text: two pillars of brass of eighteen cubits high--They were made of the brass (bronze) which was taken from the king of Zobah (Ch1 18:8). In Ch2 3:15 they are said to have been thirty-five cubits high. There, however, their joint lengths are given; whereas here the length of the pillars is given separately. Each pillar was seventeen and a half cubits long, which is stated, in round numbers, as eighteen. Their dimensions in English measure are as follows: The pillars without the capitals measured thirty-two and a half feet long, and seven feet diameter; and if hollow, as WHISTON, in his translation of JOSEPHUS, thinks (Jer 52:21), the metal would be about three and a half inches thick; so that the whole casting of one pillar must have been from sixteen to twenty tons. The height of the capitals was eight and three-fourths feet; and, at the same thickness of metal, would not weigh less than seven or eight tons each. The nature of the workmanship in the finishing of these capitals is described (Kg1 7:17-22). The pillars, when set up, would stand forty feet in height [NAPIER, Metal].
